- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.50), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect bearish sentiment’s reversal bias.
- Model frequently overshoots after recent price spikes (e.g., 73+), especially if sentiment was neutral or positive; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak.
- Mean reversion is evident in 30d forecasts: if 18-day history shows volatility, forecast should not drift too far from recent 5–7 day average.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per sentiment drop.
- For 30d horizon, avoid over-reliance on 18-day history; weight recent 5–7 days more heavily if sentiment is trending.
- Overshoots after sentiment spikes are common; apply a “lagged sentiment dampener”: subtract 0.1–0.3x the sentiment magnitude from forecast if sentiment > 0.67.
